text:
HOLLIN COUNTY SCHOOLS
Office of Special Education
PSYCHOEDUCATIONAL EVALUATION REPORT - CONFIDENTIAL

STUDENT: JAXON T. COMBS-MULLINS   DOB: 03/14/2016   AGE: 10-6
Student ID: 2031447892   Grade: 4
School: Upper Bearpen Elementary   Lunch #: 40217
Medicaid ID: 8812047356
Parent/Guardian: Brooke Mullins (mother); Chase Adkins (stepfather)
Address: 4410 Left Fork of Caney Branch Rd (RR 3 Box 212), Redbud, KY 41799
Phone: (606) 555-0143 home / 606-555-0198 mom cell   Email: bmullins82@example.com
Examiner: Tara L. Whitaker, Ed.S., NCSP, School Psychologist
Dates of Testing: 9/3/26, 9/8/26   Report Date: 09-17-2026

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Jaxon ("Jax") was referred by the Admissions and Release Committee (ARC) on 8/21/2026 after two years of Tier 3 MTSS reading intervention with limited response. His classroom teacher, Mrs. Faith Hensley, reports that Jax reads at about a 2nd grade level, avoids reading aloud, and "shuts down" when handed written work. She has faith that with the right supports he can close the gap. Attention and work completion are also concerns.

BACKGROUND / DEVELOPMENTAL HISTORY
History was obtained by phone interview with Ms. Mullins on September 3rd, 2026 and record review. Jax lives with his mother, his stepdad Chase, and his half-sister Paisley (age 6) at the head of Bunyan Holler, just past Little Caney Freewill Baptist Church, where the family attends and Jax helps his papaw, Dwight Combs, run the sound board on Sundays. His mamaw, Hope Combs, keeps the children after school and joined part of the interview. Brooke stated she has high hope the testing will "finally explain why he can't read like the other kids."

Pregnancy was full-term; Ms. Mullins disclosed prenatal tobacco exposure. Jax was slow to talk (two-word phrases at age 3). He received First Steps speech services from 2018 to 2019. From March 2022 to November 2022, J.M. was placed with a foster mom, Mrs. Dakota Pratt of Redbud, while his mother completed treatment; he returned home and the DCBS case (Case #KY-26-04471) was closed. His biological father, Hunter Combs, is not involved, though Hunter's parents (Mamaw Hope and Papaw Dwight) remain a daily support.

Medical: Jax is seen by Dr. Lyndon Ison at Laurel Fork Pediatrics for asthma (albuterol as needed). Vision and hearing screenings were passed on 08-26-2026. Dr. Ison collected Vanderbilt ratings in spring 2026 but has not diagnosed ADHD.

Jax is the only student at Upper Bearpen who shows goats at the county fair; his Boer wether placed first at the 2026 Hollin County 4-H Livestock Show. He plays third base for the Redbud Rattlers Little League, coached by Coach Gunner Ratliff, his uncle. Stepdad works for Adkins Excavating & Septic, the family business. Asked what he wants to be, Jax said "a game warden or a hunter guide like Uncle Gunner."

TESTS ADMINISTERED
Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children - Fifth Edition (WISC-V)
Kaufman Test of Educational Achievement - Third Edition (KTEA-3), Form A
Behavior Assessment System for Children - Third Edition (BASC-3): PRS-C, TRS-C, SRP-C

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS
Jax was observed in Mrs. Hensley's classroom on 9/8/26 during the ELA block. Over 30 minutes of momentary time sampling he was on task 58% of intervals (peer: 86%). He sat beside Sawyer, a peer helper, and repeatedly asked him to read directions. In testing Jax was friendly and talked readily about his goats, but fidgeted, needed redirection on timed tasks, and asked "is this almost done?" often. Results are considered valid.

TEST RESULTS
WISC-V (Mean = 100, SD = 15)
Verbal Comprehension Index (VCI)  78  7th %ile   Very Low
Visual Spatial Index (VSI)        91  27th %ile  Average
Fluid Reasoning Index (FRI)       88  21st %ile  Low Average
Working Memory Index (WMI)        76  5th %ile   Very Low
Processing Speed Index (PSI)      85  16th %ile  Low Average
Full Scale IQ (FSIQ)              82  12th %ile  Low Average

KTEA-3 (Mean = 100, SD = 15)
Letter & Word Recognition     72  3rd %ile
Reading Comprehension         70  2nd %ile
Nonsense Word Decoding        68  2nd %ile
Math Concepts & Applications  90  25th %ile
Written Expression            73  4th %ile

BASC-3 (T-scores; 60-69 At-Risk, 70+ Clinically Significant)
Scale               Parent  Teacher
Hyperactivity       64      61
Attention Problems  71      68
Anxiety             66      59
Learning Problems   --      74
Jax's SRP-C showed an elevated Sense of Inadequacy (T=67); other scales were Average.

SUMMARY AND ELIGIBILITY
Jaxon Tyler Combs-Mullins is a 10-year-old fourth grader whose overall cognitive ability falls in the Low Average range (FSIQ 82), with a relative strength in visual-spatial reasoning and weakness in working memory. Results support a pattern of strengths and weaknesses consistent with a Specific Learning Disability in basic reading skills, reading comprehension, and written expression. Attention concerns are At-Risk to Clinically Significant across settings; the ARC may consider Other Health Impairment if a diagnosis is obtained from Dr. Ison.

RECOMMENDATIONS
- Specially designed instruction in reading, 225 minutes per week in the resource setting
- Written expression SDI, 90 minutes per week in the general education classroom
- Speech-language screening with the CELF-5 given early language delay
- Sample goal: Given a 4th grade passage, the student will read orally at 90 words correct per minute with 95% accuracy by 05-20-2027.
- Accommodations: extended time (1.5x), read-aloud tests, preferential seating

The ARC meeting is scheduled for October 1st, 2026 at 3:30 p.m. Contact Mr. Dale Mason, Principal/ARC Chair, at (606) 555-0172 or dmason@example.org.

title: Speech-Language Evaluation - Kindergarten (CELF-5 / GFTA-3) - Fictional Test Record
text:
REDBUD COUNTY PUBLIC SCHOOLS
Exceptional Child Education - Speech/Language Services
SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT (CONFIDENTIAL)

STUDENT: JAXON MULLINS-COMBS            SSID: 2261049873
Legal name: Jaxon Hunter Mullins-Combs  DOB: 03/14/2020
Age at testing: 6 yrs 6 mos    Grade: K
School: Lick Branch Elementary School    Lunch #: 40318
KY Medicaid ID: 8840217735
Parent/Guardian: Faith Combs (mother); Chase Hollifield (stepfather)
Address: 1187 Upper Lick Branch Rd (Sizemore Holler), HC 64 Box 219, Cordell, KY 41788
Phone: (606) 555-0143 (mom cell)    Mamaw: 606-555-0172
Email: faith.combs86@example.com
Referral: 8/27/26    Testing: 9/16/26, 9/18/26    Report: 09-22-2026
Evaluator: Hope Adkins, M.A., CCC-SLP

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Jaxon was referred by his kindergarten teacher, Mrs. Brooke Sturgill, on August 27, 2026 after the fall BRIGANCE screen flagged the language domain. Mrs. Sturgill reports peers often cannot understand him and that he "gives up and points" when asked to repeat. Faith also asked for testing at Open House, stating that Jax's teacher at Cordell Head Start "said he'd grow out of it." Consent for evaluation was signed 8/29/26.

BACKGROUND / MEDICAL HISTORY
Sources: phone interview with Mom on 9/16/26 and records from Laurel Branch Pediatrics (Dr. Anil Varghese). Jax lives with his mother, stepdad Chase, sister Paisley (age 9, 3rd grade at Lick Branch), and baby brother Mason (14 months). Weeknights he stays with his mamaw and papaw, Loretta and Estill Combs, at the mouth of Dry Fork, because Faith works second shift as a CNA at Riverbend Nursing & Rehab in Tollivar and Chase works underground for Big Laurel Mining. His biological father, Travis Mullins, is incarcerated and has no contact. Mamaw and Papaw call him by his middle name, Hunter.

Born at 38 weeks at Tollivar Regional Medical Center. First words at about 20 months; two-word phrases after age 3. Dr. Varghese's records document seven episodes of acute otitis media between 9 months and 3 years. He was referred to Dr. Carolyn Whitt at Mountain Laurel ENT and bilateral PE tubes were placed in March 2023. Dr. Whitt removed the right tube on November 4th, 2024. Audiology at Mountain Laurel ENT on 06/10/2025 showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally.

Jax attends Little Rockhouse Old Regular Baptist Church with his grandparents, plays on the Cordell Cardinals T-ball team, and is in 4-H Cloverbuds. He is the only kindergartner who shows goats; he and Papaw showed a Nubian doeling at the Redbud County Fair in July. He is the only student in his class who rides Bus 22 from the head of the holler.

PARENT INPUT
Faith is most concerned that "people can't understand him and he gets mad." She says Paisley and his cousin Gunner (Aunt Dakota's boy, also in Mrs. Sturgill's class) "talk for him." Mamaw (Loretta Combs, by phone 9/18/26) said Hunter's words "come out all mashed together" when he's excited, and that he "talked late like his daddy."

TEACHER INPUT
Mrs. Sturgill completed a teacher checklist on 9/17/26 and was interviewed after a classroom observation on September 21st, 2026. Jax knows 14/26 uppercase letters and 9 letter sounds. Needs repetition and a visual model for two-step directions. Coach Ricky Gentry (PE and T-ball) reports no motor concerns; Coach Gentry noted J.M.C. "does fine as long as I show him."

TESTS ADMINISTERED
Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals, Fifth Edition (CELF-5)
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3), Sounds-in-Words
Language sample (52 utterances); oral mech exam; hearing screening

RESULTS
Hearing: passed 20 dB HL pure-tone screening bilaterally; Type A tympanograms.
Oral mech: adequate for speech.

CELF-5 (composite mean 100, SD 15; scaled mean 10, SD 3)
Scaled scores: Sentence Comprehension 7 / Linguistic Concepts 8 / Word Structure 5 / Word Classes 7 / Following Directions 7 / Formulated Sentences 6 / Recalling Sentences 5
Core Language Score: 77 (6th percentile, moderate)
Receptive Language Index: 83 (13th percentile)
Expressive Language Index: 74 (4th percentile)

GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words: standard score 66, 1st percentile
Error patterns: velar fronting in all positions ("cat" -> "tat," "go" -> "do"); stopping of /s/ and /f/ ("sun" -> "tun"); final consonant deletion (about 40% of opportunities); cluster reduction ("spoon" -> "poon"). Stimulable for /k/ and /g/ with tactile cues.
Intelligibility: approximately 58% to an unfamiliar listener in connected speech.

Language sample (farm-animal play): MLU 3.6 morphemes. Omits regular past tense -ed, third person -s, and auxiliary "is."
J.M.C.: "Him eat da food."
J.M.C.: "Papaw tate me to da fair."
Fluency and voice: within normal limits.

SUMMARY AND ELIGIBILITY
Jaxon presents with a moderate-to-severe phonological disorder and a moderate expressive language disorder with mild receptive involvement. The history of recurrent otitis media and PE tubes is a likely contributing factor. He appears to meet Kentucky eligibility criteria for Speech or Language Impairment; the ARC will make the final determination.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Direct speech-language therapy, 90 minutes per week (3 x 30-minute sessions), pull-out.
2. Consultation with the classroom teacher, 30 minutes per month.
3. Proposed goals:
 a. Produce /k/ and /g/ in the initial position of words with 80% accuracy across 3 consecutive sessions.
 b. Reduce final consonant deletion in CVC words to 20% or fewer occurrences in structured tasks.
 c. Use regular past tense -ed and third person -s in structured sentences with 75% accuracy.
4. Home practice folder each Friday; include Mamaw and Papaw since he stays with them weeknights. Continue annual audiology follow-up with Dr. Whitt.
5. ARC meeting: October 1, 2026, 3:15 p.m., Lick Branch Elementary School.

Hope Adkins, M.A., CCC-SLP    9/22/26
(606) 555-0198 ext. 214 | hadkins@example.org

HARLOW COUNTY SCHOOLS - OFFICE OF SPECIAL EDUCATION

Home: 4471 Right Fork of Lick Branch Rd, Poplar Gap, KY 41766 (mail to RR 2 Box 118-A)
Guardians: Loretta Caudill (maternal mamaw) and Estill Caudill (papaw)
FBA opened 9/3/26 | ARC/BIP meeting September 24th, 2026 | Review 12-10-2026
Case Manager: Mrs. Brooke Amburgey, brooke.amburgey@example.org, (606) 555-0187

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Jaxon ("Jax") was referred by the ARC after 11 office referrals between 08-13-2026 and 09-02-2026, including two bus suspensions. Jax has lived with his mamaw and papaw at the head of Coon Holler since he was nine. His mother, Faith Slone, is in residential treatment in Lexington; his stepdad, Ricky Fugate, has no contact per court order (DCBS case 26-J-0451). Mamaw reports he "shuts down and then blows up" whenever Hunter, his older half-brother, is brought up. Since Hunter's arrest this summer, Jax has been teased on the bus.

DATA SOURCES
Infinite Campus behavior log; ABC data 9/3/26 through 9/19/26 collected by Mrs. Amburgey and IA Ms. Paisley Gayheart; bus video reviewed with Transportation Director Mr. Roy Sizemore; interviews with Mr. Mason Pratt (science), Coach Darrell Sexton (PE), guardian, and student; psychological report by Dr. Renita Oakes, school psychologist, dated August 20, 2026.

ASSESSMENT SUMMARY (re-evaluation 8/20/2026)
WISC-V: FSIQ 84 (14th percentile); VCI 79; WMI 88; PSI 72
KTEA-3: Reading Comprehension SS 76; Written Expression SS 74; Math Computation SS 91
CELF-5: Core Language Score 81
BASC-3 Teacher: Externalizing Problems T=71 (Clinically Significant); Anxiety T=66 (At-Risk)
Eligibility: Emotional-Behavioral Disability, secondary Speech/Language Impairment
Medical: ADHD, combined presentation, per Dr. Wendell Hurt, Troublesome Creek Pediatrics. Methylphenidate ER 20 mg at 7:00 a.m.; mamaw says doses get missed on weekends at Aunt Hope's.

INCIDENT LOG (selected)
09/03/26 7:18 a.m. Bus 14, driver Chase Noble. A: moved to front seat; peer Gunner Tackett made "jailbird brother" comments. B: threw Chromebook, cursed driver. C: Chase stopped at the mouth of Lick Branch; papaw drove J.S.C. in. 12 min.
09-05-2026 10:40 a.m. Room 212, Mr. Pratt's science. A: asked to read lab procedure aloud. B: head down, then flipped desk. C: removed to Reset Room with Ms. Gayheart. 25 min.
Sept. 9, 2026 1:15 p.m. Gym, Coach Sexton. A: out first in dodgeball, peers laughed. B: shoved peer into bleachers. C: office referral, 1 day ISS.
9/11/26 2:55 p.m. Bus loading zone. A: waiting behind high schoolers, loud. B: refused to board, ran toward ball field. C: SRO Deputy Kendra Shepherd and Mrs. Amburgey escorted; mamaw called.
9/16/26 8:05 a.m. Room 108, resource ELA. A: independent writing prompt. B: tore worksheet, eloped. C: found in restroom, returned with break card after 9 min.
Baseline: 4.2 incidents per week; mean duration 14 minutes; 78% during reading/writing demands or unstructured transitions.

HYPOTHESIS
When given a reading or writing demand in front of peers, or teased during unstructured times (bus, gym), Jaxon engages in verbal aggression, property destruction, and elopement to escape the task and avoid peer embarrassment. More likely on Mondays and after missed medication.

STRENGTHS / INTERESTS
Polite and funny with adults one-on-one. He is the only 7th grader at LBMS who runs his own trapline; he sells muskrat pelts at the Hazard fur buy. He plays drums in the youth band at Poplar Gap Freewill Baptist Church, shows beagles with Harlow County 4-H, and works Saturdays at Caudill's Small Engine & Tire, his papaw's shop.

REPLACEMENT BEHAVIORS
1. Request a break with a break card or the cue "I need five."
2. Ask for reading help before starting written tasks.
3. On Bus 14, sit in seat 3 with headphones and give Mr. Noble a thumbs-down if a peer bothers him.
GOAL 1: Given a nonpreferred reading/writing task, Jaxon will use a replacement behavior in 4 out of 5 opportunities across 3 consecutive weeks, measured by ABC data and daily point sheets.
GOAL 2: Reduce elopement from 3 per week to 0-1 per week by 12/10/26.

PREVENTION
- No cold reading aloud; pre-teach vocabulary; text-to-speech available.
- Check-in/check-out with Mrs. Amburgey, Room 108, 7:45 and 2:40.
- Early bus release 2:50 p.m.; assigned seat 3.
- Coach Sexton assigns teams (no open picks).

REINFORCEMENT PLAN
Daily point sheet, 5 periods x 2 points. 8 of 10 points = 10 minutes of drum pad or trapping videos at end of day. 4 good days = Friday lunch with Coach Sexton. Papaw adds an extra hour in the shop for 32+ weekly points. Points are never taken away.

SERVICES

Counseling, Mountain Laurel Behavioral Health (Ms. Sawyer Brashear, LPCC): 2 x 30 minutes/month
Speech-language therapy: 60 minutes/month
Accommodations: break card, reduced written output, extended time 1.5x

CRISIS PLAN
If behavior poses imminent danger, CPI-trained staff clear the room. Restraint only per 704 KAR 7:160. Notify admin and guardian same day.

WISC-V (Dr. Farler, 3/11/26): Full Scale IQ was 84 (14th percentile); Verbal Comprehension 89, Working Memory 76, Processing Speed 78. Mr. Couch reports Jax joins discussion once he has heard the text and "knows more than he can put on paper."
Language: CELF-5 (Mrs. Slone-Ritchie, 02-24-2026) Core Language Score 77; Formulated Sentences and Understanding Spoken Paragraphs were relative weaknesses.

Feed & Hardware, where he has worked part-time since June stocking and loading feed (about 14 hrs/week). His boss, Mr. Dale Sawyer, said "Jaxon's the one I'd trust on the register if he could count change quicker." He attends Wednesday youth group at Lick Branch Freewill Baptist Church, where Brother Eli Hurt says he runs the sound board. Casey Life Skills Assessment: strengths in daily living; needs in money management and completing forms.

POSTSECONDARY GOALS
Education/Training: Within one year of graduation, Jaxon will enroll in the Diesel Technology certificate program at Redbird Valley Community and Technical College.
Employment: After training, Jaxon will work full-time as a diesel or farm equipment technician.
Independent Living: Jaxon will earn a full driver's license and manage a checking account.

AGENCY LINKAGES

Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS): job exploration counseling, workplace readiness training, paid work experience in spring. Contact rtackett@example.org, 606-555-0150.

ANNUAL GOALS (transition-related)
1. Given grade-level informational text and text-to-speech, Jaxon will identify the main idea and two supporting details with 80% accuracy on 4 of 5 weekly probes.
2. Given a mock job application and a word bank, J.B.S. will complete all required fields with no more than one error across 3 consecutive trials.
